name: Button style
first: A type of your own that draws each button it is applied to, both at rest and while it is pressed, while the button keeps its own action.

dependsOn.why: A button style draws buttons, which are controls with a label and an action.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The call `Button("Save") {}` makes a button with a label and an action, as the Save button is on the page of Control.

dependsOn.why: A button style is a type that conforms to SwiftUI's button style protocol, which requires one method.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The type `Pill` conforms to `ButtonStyle` by having `makeBody(configuration:)`, as `Friendly` conforms to `Greeter` by having `greet(name:)`.

dependsOn.why: The style draws the button's label with modifiers.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The calls `padding(8)` and `opacity` are modifiers of the label, as `padding(8)` and `opacity(0.5)` are on the page of View modifier.

what.is: A button style is a type that conforms to the protocol `ButtonStyle`. Its method `makeBody(configuration:)` gets a button's label and whether the button is pressed, and returns the view that the button is drawn as. Apple's documentation says that a button with a style still has the platform's standard behavior for a button, such as when its action runs.
what.afterExample: The style `Pill` draws a button as its label, with space around it, on yellow, and at half opacity while it is pressed. Line 17 gives the Save button that style.
what.problem: An app often wants its own look for buttons, the same on every screen. Building that look into every button repeats it, and loses the platform's behavior for presses. A button style is written once, and every button that uses it gets the look and keeps its behavior.
what.how: Apple's documentation says that the modifier `buttonStyle` sets the style for the buttons in a view and the views inside it. For each button, SwiftUI calls `makeBody(configuration:)` with a configuration: its `label`, and `isPressed`, which is true while the user presses the button. The style decides how each one looks.

when.text: Use it for the look of buttons across an app, such as a pill shape, so that every button looks and behaves the same.
Don't use it to change what a button does when tapped. Its action is the button's own, and a button style only draws it.

parts.name: The conformance to `ButtonStyle`, line 3
parts.text: The colon and the name `ButtonStyle` after `Pill` say that `Pill` conforms to the protocol `ButtonStyle`, whose one requirement is the method `makeBody(configuration:)`.

parts.name: The method `makeBody`, lines 4 to 13
parts.text: The method returns the view that the button is drawn as. Here it is the label with 8 points of padding, a yellow background, and an opacity of 0.5 while pressed and 1 otherwise.

parts.name: The configuration, line 5
parts.text: The parameter `configuration` describes one button: its `label`, the view that says what it does, and `isPressed`, which is true while the user presses it.

steps.text: Line 16 makes a button, Save, with an empty action, and line 17 gives it the style `Pill`.
Line 18 draws the button. SwiftUI calls `makeBody(configuration:)` of `Pill`, with the configuration of this button.
No one presses the button, so line 7 reads false from `isPressed`, and line 8 prints {{pressed: false}}.
Lines 9 to 12 return the label, Save, with padding, a yellow background, and an opacity of 1. While the user pressed it, `isPressed` would be true, and the button would be drawn at half opacity.

end.text: The style drew the button from its label and from whether it was pressed. The button kept its own action.
